name: rocker-blot
title: Rocker Blot
description: A waitlist capture built on a rocker blotter: submitting rocks a curved holder across the entry, lifting a fraction of its ink onto a persistent second surface whose accumulated, mirrored residue is the payoff — a physically located queue position, not a toast.
instruction: Build <RockerBlot label? buttonLabel? confirmationMessage? errorMessage? onSubmit? onReferral? className?> as a real <form> (label+input type=email autocomplete=email required, aria-describedby'd error, aria-invalid) whose canvas is a rocker-blotter ink model, aria-hidden, carrying nothing that isn't also DOM text. UPTAKE LAW, the single governing equation: uptake = max(0.04, 0.62 * exp(-age_seconds / 1.4)), where age is how long the entry string has been sitting (ms since the last keystroke) at the moment of submit — a just-typed stroke gives up ~60% density, a 3s-old one ~9%. SUBMIT SWEEP (520ms): a rocker (46px contact arc, contact point leading the geometric centre by 9px) travels min(0.62*containerWidth, 2.4*min(w,h)) px across the blotter with ±11deg rocking rotation; behind the moving boundary the ruled entry stroke under the input (canvas-drawn, its length = the submitted string's measured width in the input's own computed font, NEVER the input's own text) is redrawn at (1-uptake) density and stays that way permanently — the sweep never resets. GHOST COMPOSITE: on submit, a one-shot raster of the actual submitted string is built once (never re-rasterized per frame), mirrored horizontally (ctx.scale(-1,1)) and composited onto a SEPARATE QUEUE LATTICE — its own right-hand column (x = 0.74*containerWidth) and its own pitch (queuePitch = max(22, 0.09*min(w,h))), deliberately offset from the ambient scatter's column (x = 0.28*containerWidth, pitch = max(16, 0.055*min(w,h))) so a visitor's slot reads as a distinct stack, not one more mark in the palimpsest: y = queuePitch * queueIndex. The visitor's position in the queue is readable by eye AND is DOM text (`Position N in the queue`) inside the aria-live=polite region, because a screen reader can't count ghosts. That ghost is durable and higher-contrast than ambient ones: alpha = min(0.62, uptake * 0.7 * 1.35) plus a 1px underline, and it is NEVER cleared — the field goes read-only (not disabled) with its value intact, the button becomes disabled with an accessible name for the completed state, and returning to the section later shows the visitor's own mark. AMBIENT LAYER: 8 ghosts are seeded at mount. How OLD a blot is and how fresh the STROKE was when it was blotted are two independent axes, and conflating them is what produced an empty grey slab: seeded from one age, every mark past ~3s was deposited at the 0.04 uptake floor and rendered invisible. Seed own-ages 1/4/9/20/42/80/150/260s (blur, feather, fade) against stroke-ages 0.2/0.9/0.35/1.6/0.5/2.4/0.7/1.2s (uptake), deposit alpha = uptake * 0.95 so the sheet is never empty and always mid-process; every ghost, ambient or durable, keeps aging unconditionally in real time regardless of input: blur = 2.2 - (2.2-1.1)*exp(-ownAge/26) (3.1px dissolves an 18px mark into the paper, and the residue IS the payoff), alpha *= (1-0.04)^(ownAge/60) (4%/min decay), and 40 deterministic per-ghost fibres (mulberry32-seeded, NOT invented per frame) feather 0.5px-wide, min(9, 1.6*ownAge)px hairlines out of the raster's edges. Ambient ghosts render a deterministic cursive squiggle raster, never fabricated customer text; only the visitor's own ghost rasterizes real characters. Because five of the six seeded ages are already past the 9px feather cap at mount, a NEW ambient ghost lands on a fixed 6s cadence unconditionally — a register keeps receiving other blottings whether or not the visitor submits — which is what keeps the sheet visibly mid-process past the first ~5s AND is what eventually lets ink coverage cross the sheet-change threshold without any real submission. ROCKER IDLE: parked at the sheet's side, ±3deg over a 2.9s cosine period (peak at t=0, per spec) with 1px translation — this plus the fibre/blur/alpha drift and the 6s ambient cadence is what makes the component alive at rest indefinitely, not just for one sampled window (t=0 youngest ghost crisp ~1.4px blur; t=2.5s its edge measurably softer; t=5s softer again — all ≤0.05 alpha/s so it never competes with the field). SHEET CHANGE: when summed ghost footprint-area * alpha exceeds 34% of the sheet area, the ambient layer (not the durable/referral queue lattice) slides out over 700ms and 3 fresh ambient ghosts reseed — bounded memory, unbounded loop. REFERRAL STATE: if the consumer passes onReferral, a 'log a placeholder referral' affordance appears post-submit; each call lays a second, durable, deliberately DRIER blot (same uptake law at an age past ~4s, so it floors at 0.04) — nothing new invented for this state, it's the identical mechanic at a different age. TOKENS: read --background/--foreground/--ns-muted via getComputedStyle(documentElement) + a MutationObserver on its class, re-derive on every read which of fg/bg is the darker (by relative luminance of the resolved rgb, never by theme class name) and use that as `ink`, the other as `paper` — in light theme ink=--foreground and paper is --background nudged 4% toward --foreground (identical to the card behind it, the sheet has no edge); in dark theme ink is drawn as --background and paper is --ns-muted pulled 32% back toward --background (bare --ns-muted is a near-white slab in a dark card), so ink never inverts brighter than its paper in either theme; rebuild every ghost's raster (rasters bake ink in as pixels) when tokens change. --ns-accent is the submit button fill and focus rings only, never the ink or a ghost. prefers-reduced-motion composes one still frame at STATIC_TIME=1.90s of a DEMONSTRATION blot (not a real submission): rocker 63% across its travel at -7deg, the entry stroke lifted behind/full ahead, a fresh ghost landing at 0.44 alpha over five deterministic older ghosts solved to sit at exactly 1.9/2.3/2.7/2.9/3.1px blur. Every ghost age and the sweep fraction are computed against ONE frozen clock value captured once (never performance.now() read again inside the static path, including on resize) so the frame is byte-stable indefinitely, not just for the first ~200ms. SHEET: inset 12px from the canvas on every side with a 5px rounded edge, a hairline --ns-muted border, a deterministic fibre speckle and the shading the rocker bar casts along its top edge — a full-bleed flat fill reads as a broken image, not as paper. Every ghost is clipped to that outline. The rocker is drawn as a body (curved shoe + handle) resting ON the sheet, not as two bare arcs floating above it. Canvas: ResizeObserver on the host (not window), DPR capped at 2, IntersectionObserver + visibilitychange pause the rAF, no paint before the first successful token read on the rAF-start, resize and intersection-resume paths alike.
useWhen: Pick rocker-blot for a landing-page email/waitlist capture that needs a real, durable payoff instead of a toast — the queue position and the accumulating residue ARE the confirmation. Pick signature-consent instead when the surface is an authorization/consent capture whose captured mark must stay exactly as drawn; pick streaming-ink-dry instead when the surface is read-only status text arriving and settling in place, with nothing subtracted or moved to a second surface.
